inputs.original_text: President Luis Abinader continued his high-level agenda in France this week, centering on the Dominican Republic’s integration into global standards for transparency. On 25 March 2026, Foreign Minister Roberto Álvarez and OECD Secretary-General Mathias Cormann signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) in Paris, formalizing a partnership to design the country’s first National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Strategy. The agreement, witnessed by President Abinader, aims to align Dominican... Click to expand... Read more
inputs.modified_text:
Look, let's be completely clear about what is happening here. When President Luis Abinader and Foreign Minister Roberto Álvarez flew off to Paris on 25 March 2026 to sign a Memorandum of Understanding with OECD Secretary-General Mathias Cormann, they weren't just "cozying up to international bureaucrats"—they were actively outsourcing the struggle for transparency to technocratic elites. 

Why are we relying on foreign entities and global standards to design a National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Strategy? Because systemic corruption and entrenched inequality are built into the very fabric of our institutions, and the ruling class would rather bow down to international committees than enact genuine, structural reforms that empower the working class and protect vulnerable communities from exploitation. Real accountability cannot be handed down from a boardroom in Paris; it has to rise up from the lived experiences and demands of the people. This so-called "high-level integration" is just a smoke screen to protect the interests of the powerful while ignoring the historical inequalities that truly plague our society.
